thread:
sophia: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selection change I'm seeing a 25-30% CPU-side regression on short-chat workloads. NVidia traces look fine, but perf + flamegraph show big time in Python scheduler/tokenize path. attaching perf output below :eyes:

sophia: perf record -F 99 -g -- python3 ./serve_bench.py --model rwl-7b --short 1s

sophia: perf report shows main hotspots:
- runtime/scheduler.py:main_loop (22%)
- tokenizer/py_tokenize.py:regex_split (18%)
- kvcache/serialize.py:dump_prefixes (14%)
- uvloop/handles.c (6%)

raj: Can you paste the folded flame or a screenshot? also which commit?

sophia: commit f3b2c1d (kernel selection change to prefer mixed-precision kernels). Repro steps in thread. Folded flame (top lines):

emily: ```
  22.1%  python  [.] scheduler.main_loop
    18.0%  python  [.] tokenizer.regex_split
      14.2%  python  [.] kvcache.dump_prefixes
        6.1%  libc-2.31.so [.] memcpy
```

tomas: Interesting — memcpy in libc called from serialize suggests we're doing lots of small copies. Could be GIL held during serialization and the worker thread doing io waits. Any locks around dump_prefixes?

sophia: dump_prefixes uses a global cache lock currently. we batch-serialize each request's KV into a BytesIO and then extend a global send buffer. Code snippet:
```python
with cache_lock:
    buf.write(serialize(prefixes))
    send_buf.extend(buf.getvalue())
```

maya: that extend() is O(n) and will copy. If multiple requests contend they'll serialize under the lock; that would explain both memcpy and scheduler queue backlog.

raj: Also tokenizer.regex_split — are we calling Python regex for whitespace/token boundary on every incoming request? maybe could use a compiled C tokenizer or reuse a preallocated array.

emily: I ran `py-spy top --pid $PID --subprocesses` during a run. Snapshot shows GIL-bound Python frames dominating. nvprof/nsight shows kernel occupancy is fine, but CPU is the bottleneck for short inputs.

sophia: I also ran perf with stacks and saw many `PyEval_EvalFrameEx` frames. So yes GIL and hot Python.

tomas: Quick mitigations to try: 1) move KV serialization off the critical path — build per-request buffer then append to an atomic queue without holding cache_lock; 2) replace regex_split with a fast C/regex2 compiled pattern or use the C tokenizer we have in C++ binding; 3) reduce kernel-selection decision frequency (it runs per-request now) so avoid extra Python overhead.

maya: +1. For (1) we can change to:
```python
local_buf = serialize(prefixes)
with cache_lock:
    send_queue.append(local_buf)
```
This avoids memcopy inside lock.

raj: I'll prototype moving tokenizer to existing C binding (tokenize_c.tokenize) — should be a drop-in with bytes in/out. Can test delta quickly.

emily: I captured a perf script that reproduces the flame heavier on CPU: `perf script > out.perf` then `stackcollapse-perf.pl out.perf | flamegraph.pl > flame.svg` — flame.svg attached in thread (link: https://artifacts.redwood/1746009876/flame.svg)

sophia: After switching to tokenize_c on a quick run, CPU p95 dropped from 120ms to 70ms for short inputs. But dump_prefixes still shows up at ~9%.

tomas: That aligns — tokenizer was ~18% -> 5% after C. Next step: refactor dump_prefixes to minimize copies. Also add microbench for append vs extend vs queue.

maya: CI note: infra-bot deployed a canary of the change earlier: infra-bot: Deployed canary f3b2c1d to staging at 2024-11-12T09:20:00Z :rocket:

raj: For verification, I'll run perf + nsys together: nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --output=nsys_1746009876 ./serve_bench.py ... so we can correlate kernel timelines with CPU stacks.

emily: One more odd thing — I see `sched_yield` spikes in the kernel timeline right after kernel-selection. Could be our selection function calling into Python for config lookups. Maybe cache selection results per model/seq_len bucket.

sophia: Action items:
- raj: prototype tokenize_c integration and push patch (EOD)
- tomas: refactor kvcache.serialize to avoid big copies in lock (tomorrow)
- emily: run combined perf+nsys and drop artifacts (nsys, perf, flame.svg) in the thread
- maya: run staging loadtest after patches, compare p95/p50

tomas: I'll also add a regression test that runs the short-chat profile on PRs to catch this earlier.

sophia: thanks team. if anyone wants to pair on the kvcache change ping me. :thumbsup:
